6.0: (Se'if Katan 7) "That we do not, etc." Likewise, this ruling appears in the Tur, which copied the law concerning foods that come after the meal. The Beit Yosef writes that even though the Rosh stated that this practice is not common among us, the Tur holds that in large meals, even among us, it is common for people to withdraw their hands from the bread at the end of the meal.
6.1: "Our custom follows the words of the Tosafot." This means that while from the Rosh’s wording it could be inferred that only in an ordinary meal—where bread is not removed until after Birkat HaMazon—do we not withdraw from the bread until after the blessing, in large meals where the bread is removed before Birkat HaMazon, we too remove and withdraw from the bread. However, from the wording of Tosafot, it appears that even if the bread is removed before Birkat HaMazon, our custom is still not to withdraw from the bread. Therefore, even in large meals, people do not withdraw from the bread, and we rely on the Tosafot. Thus, it would appear as a separate meal—this is the correct reading.
